purpose: Enforced transfer-size budget for the website's client bundle. Enforced by tests/bundle-budget.test.mjs, which runs as part of `npm test` and CI.
rationale: Audit #2 (docs/audit/MASTER_AUDIT.md) scored performance engineering 25/100 — the repository's weakest area — because no performance measurement of any kind existed. Three skills discussed performance; nothing measured it.

Budgets below were set from a real measurement of the 2026-08-07 build, not from a generic recommendation. Headroom is deliberately modest (~15%) so a genuine regression fails rather than being absorbed silently.
Sizes are gzip, not raw: Cloudflare negotiates compression on every asset response, so gzip is the honest proxy for what a visitor actually downloads. Raw sizes are recorded for reference only.

This is a transfer-size budget, NOT a Core Web Vitals budget. LCP/INP/CLS still have no measurement in this repository — see MASTER_AUDIT.md finding H-1. Do not read a passing budget as a passing performance gate.
whenExceeded: Do not raise the budget as the first response. Establish why the bundle grew.
A new dependency is the usual cause — check whether it is actually needed (the gsap removal in .solo/tasks.md T11 is the precedent).
Raise a budget only with a recorded justification in .solo/decisions.md, and update measuredBaseline in the same change.
